title: Reword the 42 phrases on Daniel's screens that he would have to stop and decode
ask:
The plain-language check became a judgement pass on 2026-09-19 (it reads docs/WRITING.md and docs/writing_rulings.json and decides the way a careful colleague would, instead of matching a list of 23 banned words). On its first full run it read 423 pieces of text on the screens Daniel actually looks at and objected to 80 of them: 42 he would have to stop and work out, 38 worth a second look.

All 80 were recorded as known so they do not fail the build — a red build has to mean something broke, not that a backlog exists — but they are still on his screens, which is the whole point of the check. Work through them. Each one below carries the phrase the judge objected to, why, and a suggested rewrite; the suggestion is a starting point, not an instruction, and several will be better solved by saying the thing a different way entirely. Run `python3 tools/check_writing.py` after each batch: a reworded sentence is a new one to the check, so it gets judged fresh and loses its grandfathering automatically.

Two cautions. Do not reword anything that is the name of something in the game or on the roadmap — the Mark III, the overnight, phase 4 and the rest are names Daniel coined, and the judge has been taught to leave them alone; if one of those shows up below, the brief needs another ruled-fine example rather than the text needing a change. And where the judge is simply wrong, add the sentence to `ruled_fine` in docs/writing_rulings.json with the reason — that is how the standard gets sharper, and --self-test will hold it there.

THE FINDINGS:

- hq/data/goals/product.json
  text: I need absolute trust in the progress we're making, as reported on the program report. If I can't trust the data, then I can use the program report. I
  objection: “If I can't trust the data, then I can use the program report.” — The sentence contradicts itself; 'can't trust the data' should lead to 'can't use the program report,' but it says 'can use.'
  suggested: If I can't trust the underlying data, I have nothing reliable to work from.
- hq/data/goals/sales.json
  text: Nothing measurable is stopping a tag; monitoring is still landing on {unassured} of {total} checks a release has to pass, and the plans are filed.
  objection: “monitoring is still landing on {unassured} of {total} checks” — The word 'landing' is internal process vocabulary; a reader would have to ask what state these checks are in.
  suggested: checks are still being fielded for {unassured} of {total}
- hq/data/work/w16cb59a1b8f.json
  text: Add the ground-line finding to the notes for the art style session
  objection: “ground-line finding” — This compound term is unexplained specialized vocabulary—a stranger has no way to know what a ground-line finding is or why it belongs in art-session notes.
  suggested: the finding about where the ground sits in the frame
- hq/data/work/w3e5997f5065.json
  text: A project can be deferred by a ruling without reading as stuck
  objection: “reading as stuck” — The phrasing is unclear: does 'reading' mean 'appearing'? This costs a re-read to parse.
  suggested: without appearing stuck
- hq/data/work/w5c0a9f21e3b7.json
  text: Seven senses measure across the page boundary with nothing stopping them
  objection: “Seven senses measure across the page boundary with nothing stopping them” — Multiple unexplained elements compound: what are 'senses'? What does it mean for them to 'measure across the page boundary'? The sentence assumes design vocabulary Daniel holds but a reader does not.
  suggested: Seven [if this is an entity name, introduce it: 'The seven senses, a subsystem that...'] reach across the page boundary unobstructed
- hq/data/work/w68bb0410cb06.json
  text: The nameplate and the likes-and-dislikes grid
  objection: “The nameplate and the likes-and-dislikes grid” — This is a sentence fragment with no verb—what is supposed to happen to these UI elements? A reader cannot tell whether the work is to build, review, adjust, or decide on them.
  suggested: Pair the nameplate and the likes-and-dislikes grid on the robot card
- hq/data/work/w97ad146c93d.json
  text: Point Jade's overnight-loop item at the watering inset's loader
  objection: “Point Jade's overnight-loop item at the watering inset's loader” — Technical jargon ('Point at', 'loader') and unclear what entity is being modified make this require decoding.
  suggested: Update the overnight loop to load its resources the same way the watering inset does
- hq/data/work/w9f46b7286df.json
  text: The robot ladder's bottom two rungs: the mark-1 arrives when the work has been felt, the mark-2 once a mark-1 has been used
  objection: “when the work has been felt” — Felt is metaphorical; the reader doesn't know whether this means experienced, understood, or something else.
  suggested: when the player has experienced the problem it solves
- hq/data/work/wc84b2f6e913.json
  text: Tuned values cannot be made the real render
  objection: “Tuned values cannot be made the real render” — The reader would need to work out what 'tuned values' means and what 'made the real render' means — these are internal mechanism terms, not consequences.
  suggested: Parameter tweaks must not change the rendered frame
- hq/data/work/wdfa69cafdc98.json
  text: What it sees, live, and the bars showing what it is about to do
  objection: “What it sees, live, and the bars showing what it is about to do” — Bare pronoun 'it' has no referent in the sentence — a reader would have to ask what 'it' is.
  suggested: The robot sees this, live: the bars showing what it is about to do
- hq/static/app.js
  text: Out of tokens until about . Keep typing — anything you send is queued here and answered automatically when the window reopens.
  objection: “Out of tokens until about” — Same issue as [16]: the timestamp is missing, and a reader of this status message needs to know when.
  suggested: Out of tokens until [time]. Keep typing — anything you send is queued here and answered automatically when the window reopens.
- hq/static/pillars.js
  text: thing open here — mine to handle.
  objection: “thing open here — mine to handle” — Two vague nouns: a reader would have to ask what the thing is and what 'open' means.
  suggested: I'm handling [specific item]: [why it is waiting]
- hq/static/pillars.js
  text: not prepped — owes you a card on this before it is fair to ask
  objection: “owes you a card on this” — Card is internal HQ vocabulary for a decision record or work item; a stranger cannot tell what it means.
  suggested: someone needs to prepare a decision on this before proceeding
- hq/static/pillars.js
  text: My goals I have not declared goals for this area yet, so nothing here is being measured.
  objection: “My goals I have not declared goals” — The statement structure is ambiguous—it reads as a fragment followed by a different sentence; a reader must reparse to find the meaning.
  suggested: I have not set goals for this area yet, so nothing is being measured
- hq/static/pillars.js
  text: : ", length not recorded on the project"}
  objection: “: ", length not recorded on the project"}” — This is a JSON or data structure fragment; it appears to be code leaking through and is not readable as human text.
  suggested: [This should not appear to users—it indicates a broken data structure or error state]
- hq/static/pillars.js
  text: No such pillar. Dashboard
  objection: “No such pillar. Dashboard” — Dashboard appears as a lone word with no clear relationship to the sentence before it—is it a button, an instruction, or incomplete text?
  suggested: This pillar does not exist. Open the Dashboard.

  objection: “).join("") : " Nothing this week. ")}” — This is template or code syntax mixed with text; it is not readable as human prose.

- hq/static/pillars.js

  objection: “margin-top:8px; display:flex; gap:6px” — This is CSS styling notation, not human text.
  suggested: [This should not appear to users]
- hq/static/pillars.js

  objection: “GitHub CI the only result” — The sentence is missing a verb—should be 'GitHub CI is the only result'; a reader must reparse to find meaning.
  suggested: GitHub CI is the only result someone outside the studio can check on the commit itself
- hq/static/pillars.js
  text: Every CI run on main — oldest on the left passed, failed of the last finished runs · green in a row right now. Failures clustered on one day are an in
  objection: “oldest on the left passed, failed of the last finished runs · green in a row right now” — Grammar is broken; 'failed of the last finished runs' is not a complete clause, and 'green in a row' is ambiguous about what it counts.
  suggested: The oldest run passed, but recent runs have failed · currently green runs hold
- hq/static/pillars.js
  text: No recorded session says who played it or whether they had been coached, so that open bar could be a real miss or a tester who had already been shown 
  objection: “so that open bar could be a real miss or a tester who had already been shown the cot” — 'That open bar' refers to a visual element the reader cannot see from the text alone.
  suggested: so this gap could be a real miss in onboarding, or a tester who had already seen the cot
- hq/static/pillars.js
  text: 0 recorded sessions carry their conditions
  objection: “0 recorded sessions carry their conditions” — 'Carry their conditions' is cryptic — the reader must guess what this means.
  suggested: No recorded sessions include their test conditions
- hq/static/pillars.js
  text: The next public release — the next public release — ships as once the onboarding checklist passes on a sitting with a brand-new player, and the tag go
  objection: “The next public release — the next public release — ships as once the onboarding checklist passes on a sitting with a brand-new player, and the tag goes out. of steps done on its critical work.” — Repeated phrase, 'ships as once' is grammatically wrong, 'sitting' is unclear, and 'of steps done' is a sentence fragment.
  suggested: The next public release ships once the onboarding checklist passes with a new player, then the tag goes out.
- hq/static/pillars.js
  text: Scored on a build that cannot be resolved any more.
  objection: “Scored on a build that cannot be resolved any more” — 'Cannot be resolved' is ambiguous — resolved in what sense, and why does it affect this score?

  objection: “Scored on a build commits behind what you would ship today” — Grammar is incomplete — missing the link between 'build' and 'commits behind'.

  objection: “After this one, on the board, still being scoped — see the program” — 'After this one' has no referent, and 'the program' is undefined.
  suggested: The next card is on the board and still being scoped
- hq/static/pillars.js

  objection: “— % of taps did nothing” — The percentage value is missing — this is incomplete data.

  objection: “The sheets could not be read” — Undefined term — which sheets, and in what format?

- hq/static/pillars.js
  text: colours across shipped sheets, widest first by how much of the game is that colour. The notched ones are the the style guide names — of them are still
  objection: “The notched ones are the the style guide names — of them are still in the build” — Typo ('the the'), incomplete opening, and 'of them' is unclear (should name which ones).

  text: s own note says its ramps were measured from a sprite pack that is no longer in this repo. So this is not necessarily drift in the art — it may be a g

  objection: “The launch check — of monitored To publish, from a terminal:” — The phrase 'of monitored To publish' does not parse — it appears to have lost words or been mangled. A reader cannot work out what is meant.

  text: ; }).join("")} 🟩 productive · 🟨 satisfied ("already done") · 🟥 wasted — one column per minute. A red streak is where she was lost; a gap is a break. F
  objection: “where she was lost” — Bare pronoun 'she' is not introduced in the sentence; 'lost' also lacks context—lost in what sense?

  objection: “That is the one a player has to notice from across the plot.” — The bare pronoun 'the one' has no referent in this sentence — a reader would have to work back to prior context.

  objection: “in the cell on screen.” — Standing alone, this fragment is too isolated for a reader to understand what condition it describes.

first_action: Run python3 tools/check_writing.py to see the current list, and start with hq/static/*.js, where the text is on screen for him every time he opens the dashboard.
source_message: The first run of the new judgement-based plain-language check. Filed rather than fixed in place because several are wording calls on his own surfaces.
